A1.justification: Both readable ten-page PDFs describe the same PhD benchmark and provide corresponding methods, tables, figures, and references. Neither contains an appendix or embedded supplement; separately mentioned supplementary prompts are outside the supplied material.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original benchmark evaluations of ten open-source MLLMs and GPT-4o, including quantitative results and qualitative examples.

after.justification: Section 4 retains original evaluations and adds results for further MLLMs and hallucination-mitigation methods.

M1.justification: The ChatGPT-assisted construction pipeline, CLIP-based hitem selection, context generation, and CCS image generation remain unchanged. PhD-iac becomes PhD-sec without changing its procedure. Replacing CLIP with stronger encoders is only suggested; VCD and Woodpecker are evaluated comparators.

E1.justification: The five tasks, four evaluation modes, TDIUC/MS-COCO images, CCS images, and POPE/AMBER evaluations are retained. The terminology change introduces no new scenario. Newly discussed benchmarks such as ROME are not added to the experimental coverage.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds LLaVA-OneVision, Molmo, InternVL-1.5, Cambrian-1, LLaVA-1.6-XL, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Gemini 1.5 Pro. It also evaluates VCD and Woodpecker with Qwen-VL and LLaVA-1.6-L. POPE/AMBER comparisons now include the previously omitted InstructBLIP variants, mPLUG-Owl2, and MiniGPT-v2.

E3.justification: Added evaluations introduce model configurations up to 72B parameters. VCD uses full-set evaluation, while Woodpecker and the additional proprietary models use random-2k. Existing prompting and scoring remain unchanged. The newly specified POPE-adversarial and AMBER-discriminative variants do not establish that earlier settings changed.

E4.justification: Existing diagnostic analyses are updated: Table 6 replaces Qwen-VL/LLaVA-1.6-L profiles with LLaVA-OneVision/Molmo profiles, and Figure 3 replaces the CCS camel-counting example with a tire-shape example and changes participating models. Answer-tendency analysis covers more models, while Figure 5 retains the same 7B-versus-13B analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions use Spearman correlation and retain the same statistical plot types. V4 adds no reported repeated-run counts, seeds, significance tests, or new uncertainty-reporting procedures. The revised correlation coefficient is a result change.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds substantial results, including PhD scores of 0.698 for LLaVA-OneVision, 0.690 for Molmo, and 0.746 for Claude 3.5 Sonnet; retained Table 5 PhD scores stay unchanged. POPE entries change, including Qwen-VL from 0.86 to 0.83, but v3 leaves the benchmark variant unspecified. Table 6 replaces model profiles. For the expanded model set, mean open-model say-yes rate changes from 0.691 to 0.611 and Spearman correlation from -0.99 to -0.92. Table 4 doubles CCS task counts to match the unchanged 750 Yes/750 No totals.

T1.justification: The PhD Index remains the harmonic mean of Yes and No recalls. V4 adds the explanatory random-guess reference of 0.5, without introducing a new mathematical definition, derivation, assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: The benchmark, pipeline, and diagnostic contributions remain intact. The introduction expands the empirical contribution to include mitigation methods, and the conclusion replaces Qwen-VL/LLaVA-1.6-L/MiniGPT-v2 with LLaVA-OneVision/Molmo/InternVL-1.5 as the leading open-source models.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 newly suggests stronger vision encoders for future hitem selection. Sections 4.3–4.4 replace Qwen-VL-focused explanations and refinement priorities with discussion of LLaVA-OneVision and Molmo, particularly sentiment and counting weaknesses. The broader visual-ambiguity, textual-bias, and internal-knowledge interpretations remain.

D1.justification: V4 adds a project repository address and removes v3's peer-review supplementary-dataset notice. Table 5 specifies benchmark variants and documents the new models' encoders and LLMs. Section 4.3 removes the earlier explicit LLaVA input-resolution examples; both versions still refer readers elsewhere for additional prompts.

R1.justification: Sections 1–2 and Tables 1–2 add ROME, WHOOPS!, VLind-Bench, and GAVIE, including a substantive comparison with ROME's CCS construction. References for newly evaluated models and mitigation methods are added. The central positioning around objective, low-/middle-level visual hallucination evaluation remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 consistently renames inaccurate context/PhD-iac to specious context/PhD-sec, makes localized prose and caption revisions, updates author information, and adds acknowledgements. The main section order and narrative organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The empirical displays are substantially reworked. Table 5 gains separate full-set/random-2k blocks, Figure 3 is recomposed with additional model columns, and Figure 4 adds an overall-index series and subset indicators. Figure 6 revises its axes and legend, while Table 6 and Figure 5 are relocated.

improvement.justification: V4 strengthens benchmark validation through more competitive models, mitigation comparisons, and previously missing POPE/AMBER results. Corrected CCS statistics and clearer evaluation grouping improve accuracy and transparency. Some older diagnostic profiles are replaced, and differing full-set/random-2k samples still limit direct comparisons, so the overall quality gain is useful but limited.
